title: What Does a Carpet Warranty Actually Cover?
meta: A carpet warranty covers fiber wear, texture loss and listed stains, not traffic lanes or pet damage. What Seattle homeowners can claim. Wills Flooring.
keywords: what does a carpet warranty cover, carpet warranty exclusions, carpet wear warranty explained, carpet stain warranty claim, carpet installation Seattle WA

blocks.lead: A carpet warranty covers three narrow things: the fiber wearing away by more than a stated percentage, the texture matting beyond a rated level, and specific food and beverage stains that will not clean out. It does not cover crushing in traffic lanes, pet urine, fading, seams or anything the maker can blame on the pad or the cleaning schedule.
blocks.detail: Add the installer's workmanship warranty, a separate document, and you have the whole picture. Ours runs 1 year on top of the mill's coverage. Our labor is published too, $0.99 per sq ft stretch-in and $30 per step, which matters when a remedy covers the carpet but not the labor to lay it.

blocks.html: Seattle buyers read the sample tag in a Ballard living room, see a 20-year or lifetime warranty, and assume the carpet is guaranteed for 20 years. Then the hall in a Queen Anne rental looks flat after four years and the claim is denied. The tag was not lying, it was describing something far narrower than people think. Here is each warranty type, what voids it, and how a claim really goes.

blocks.text: The four warranties on a carpet label

items.title: Abrasive wear
items.text: The fiber must lose more than a set percentage of its pile weight, usually 10 percent, in one area. That means fiber physically gone, measured in a lab. Flattened, dull or discolored pile is not wear, and this is the warranty most people think they have.

items.title: Texture retention
items.text: The mill rates the carpet on a matting and crushing scale, and the claim succeeds if yours drops below that rating. In practice it is judged from photos and a site visit, and traffic lanes are almost always called soiling instead.

items.title: Stain and soil
items.text: Coverage is for a listed set of food and drink stains that resist proper cleaning. Typical exclusions: pet urine, vomit, bleach, hair dye, mustard, hot beverages and anything strongly dyed. Soil coverage is about dry dirt, not the gray look of a lane.

items.title: Installation workmanship
items.text: This is the installer's, not the mill's. It covers seams opening, ripples from a loose stretch and transitions coming up. Ours runs 1 year, and it is the one that gets used, because most first-year problems are installation, not fiber.

blocks.text: What the fine print excludes, in almost every brand

head: Problem you see
Covered?
Why not
rows: Traffic lane in the hall looks darker and flatter
Classified as soiling and crushing from use. Only a measured drop below the rating counts.
Dog urine spot that will not come out
Excluded from nearly all stain warranties unless you bought a pet-labeled product, and even those require prompt cleaning.
Fading by a south window in West Seattle
Sunlight and ozone fading are excluded. Solution-dyed fiber resists it better, but it is not covered.
Carpet on stairs wearing at the nose
Most wear warranties exclude stairs entirely or cut the coverage period in half.
Seam showing or ripples after a year
Workmanship. The mill points you to whoever installed it, which is why that warranty matters.
blocks.note: Every brand words these differently. Read the warranty PDF for the product you are buying, not the sample tag.

blocks.html: Do this before you lean on a long warranty number. A Queen Anne upstairs of 900 sq ft with a 15-step staircase is 900 × $0.99 + 15 × $30 = $891 + $450 = $1,341 in labor, plus $0.45 per sq ft to pull and haul the old carpet, plus carpet and pad from the estimate. A prorated remedy that hands you replacement carpet and nothing toward labor leaves you paying that $1,341 again.

blocks.text: The conditions that quietly void coverage

items.html: The wrong pad. Nearly every warranty sets a minimum pad density and a maximum thickness. A thick, soft pad from a big-box bundle can void the texture warranty on day one. We match the pad to the mill spec and note it on the quote. More in our carpet padding explainer.
No professional cleaning receipts. Most warranties require extraction by a certified cleaner every 12 to 24 months, with proof. No receipts, no claim. Set the reminder the day the carpet goes in.
The wrong cleaning method. Some brands exclude damage from rental machines or unapproved cleaners. Check before you rent one.
Installed in an excluded room. Stairs, bathrooms and commercial use are commonly excluded, and a Capitol Hill condo run as a short-term rental can count as commercial.
Losing the invoice. Some warranties transfer only to the original buyer and require the dated invoice with the style number. Keep ours with the house papers.

blocks.text: How a claim actually plays out

items.d: Step 1: call the installer, not the mill
items.text: Most year-one problems are stretch, seams or transitions, and those are on us. We come out and fix workmanship issues under the 1-year warranty at no charge.

items.d: Step 2: document before you clean again
items.text: Photos in daylight, the invoice, the style number off a leftover piece and your cleaning receipts. Note where the problem is and when you first saw it.
The mill sends an independent inspector who measures pile height, takes a sample and checks the pad. In Seattle that takes a few weeks to schedule, and the report goes to the mill, so ask for a copy.
If approved, the usual remedy is replacement carpet of comparable value, prorated by age, sometimes with a labor allowance. Full refunds are rare, and labor at $0.99 per sq ft is often yours to pay.

blocks.text: Mistakes that turn a good carpet into a denied claim

a.title: Do this
items: Buy the pad the mill specifies, not the thickest one on the shelf
Book hot-water extraction every 12 to 18 months and keep the receipt
Keep the invoice, style number and a leftover scrap
Report seams and ripples to your installer in the first year

b.title: Avoid this
items: Assuming a lifetime tag means the carpet will look new for life
Letting pet accidents sit overnight, then claiming a stain defect
Putting bedroom-grade carpet on a Wallingford staircase and expecting stair coverage
Buying online with no installer, so nobody owns the workmanship

blocks.title: A Seattle note on condos and rentals:
blocks.text: Many Capitol Hill and Belltown buildings require carpet in bedrooms for sound. If you rent the unit out, some mills reclassify the use as commercial and shorten coverage. Ask us to check the wording before you buy for a rental.
What to ask before you sign for carpet

items: Which warranties apply to this exact style, and for how many years each.
Whether stairs are covered, and for how long.
Which pad density and thickness the mill requires, and whether the quote uses it.
How often professional cleaning is required and what counts as proof.
What the installer's workmanship warranty covers and for how long. Ours is 1 year, in writing.
Who you call first when something goes wrong. It should be a local number; ours is (425) 350-4435.

faq.q: Does a carpet wear warranty cover matting and crushing?
faq.a: Not the wear warranty. Wear means fiber physically lost, usually more than 10 percent of pile weight in one area. Matting and crushing fall under a separate texture retention warranty, judged against the carpet's rated level. Traffic-lane flattening is usually called soiling, so it is the hardest claim to win.

faq.q: Are pet stains covered by carpet stain warranties?
faq.a: Almost never under a standard stain warranty. Pet urine, feces and vomit are listed exclusions for most brands. Some pet-specific lines do cover them, but they require prompt cleaning and the specified pad. If you have dogs or cats, buy a product that names pets in its warranty.

faq.q: Do I really need professional cleaning to keep a carpet warranty?
faq.a: Yes for most brands. The typical requirement is hot-water extraction by a professional every 12 to 24 months, with dated receipts as proof. Skipping it is one of the most common reasons a claim gets denied, whatever the fiber actually did.

faq.q: Is carpet on stairs covered by the warranty?
faq.a: Usually not, or only for a shorter period. Stairs concentrate wear on the nose of each tread, so most mills exclude them or halve the coverage. If a Seattle staircase is a big part of the job, choose a dense nylon and treat stair wear as maintenance, not a warranty item.

faq.q: What does the installer's workmanship warranty cover?
faq.a: Problems from the installation itself: seams peaking or opening, ripples from a loose stretch, transitions lifting and tack strip issues. Wills Flooring covers those for 1 year at no charge. It is separate from the mill's fiber warranties and is the one most likely to be used.

faq.q: What do I actually get if a carpet warranty claim is approved?
faq.a: Usually replacement carpet of comparable quality, prorated by how many years you have had it, sometimes with a contribution toward labor. Cash refunds are rare. Our labor is $0.99 per sq ft, so you can price what a prorated remedy would still leave you paying.
